tips.li: USAC trades in credit bonds rather than the silver everyone else on the rim uses.
When trading with USAC merchants, make sure your sealed bags are inside trade beacon range.
Body bags only store and transport corpses - they don't preserve them. Build cold storage to slow decay, because USAC will not buy rotten corpses.
A body bag's value depends on the condition of the corpse inside. Recovering bodies quickly and refrigerating them pays far better than leaving them out in the open.
Only bags that already contain a corpse count toward your currency. Empty bags are worth nothing in trade.
USAC trades in credit bonds rather than the silver everyone else on the rim uses.
USAC takes bonds first in any trade. Buying new bonds with bonds can incur a "depreciation fee," so keep your reserves in a vault with its trade beacon switched off.
A credit bond is issued at a value of 1000, but dealers sell them at a premium. How large that premium is depends on your goodwill with USAC.
Most USAC services draw bonds from trade beacon range only, not from your whole map. Keep reserves outside beacon range if you want them left alone.
If you run debt contracts and leased services on the same map, keep a buffer of spare bonds so the two don't collide on settlement day.
USAC charges interest every 30 days - one corporate quarter. Make sure your colony has enough credit bonds on hand when settlement day arrives.
Repaying more than 10% of the total principal in a single quarter incurs a surcharge that scales with the amount.
If you can't pay down the principal, at least keep enough income coming in to cover the quarterly interest.
USAC grants two grace periods on unpaid interest. The third default triggers forced collection.
If your debt is about to become unpayable, consider leaving this planet while you still can.
Heavy mining rigs pollute continuously while they run. Planning cleanup and isolation zones early keeps the mess away from your colony core.
Heavy mining rig leases can be extended with bonds. If money is tight, keep the rig running and rebuild your reserves next trade cycle.
Mech readiness falls over time, and very low readiness carries penalties. Steady resupply beats emergency refits.
Each resupply restores about 25% of a mech's maximum readiness. A dedicated resupply area with parts on hand cuts frontline downtime sharply.
Air-dropped USAC units and equipment need clear ground to land on. If your base is crowded, keep some open tiles in reserve so drops don't fail or drift.
